validated_work_order.understanding: The weekly end-bound suite exists twice and runs twice on every test run. packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/weekly-end-date.test.ts is 338 lines with 10 `it(...)`; custom-spreadsheet.test.ts is 1100 lines and carries all ten of those titles under `weekly custom report end bound` (line 380, seven cases) and `weekly grouped report end bound` (line 504, three cases). I re-verified every technical claim against the files in this checkout rather than carrying v2's finding over. The ten `it('...')` titles extracted from each file are identical. Diffing the two describe blocks returns 76 changed lines, and filtering those 76 lines for `expect|toEqual|toBe|toHave` returns nothing: no assertion, expected value or snapshot line differs anywhere. Every hunk is the props wrapper alone, `runCustom({...})` against `runCustom(weeklyProps({...}))`. The split is 7/3 in both files. The weeklyRows fixture is byte-identical (md5 6342ab83b4f60f70b3f77d129ec0d601 in both). weeklyProps supplies precisely the defaults the shorter file's own runCustom already defaulted to, plus `balanceTypeOp: undefined`, which sortData.ts:24 already guards with `if (!balanceTypeOp || !sortByOp) return () => 0`. So the comparison the epic asked for resolves one way: weekly-end-date.test.ts contributes no unique case and is deleted outright, nothing folded back. A repo-wide grep for 'weekly-end-date' returns no hit in any source, config or CI file, and vitest discovers tests by the glob at vite.config.mts:406, so nothing has to be unlisted along with the deletion.

This version fixes three ways in which v2 contradicted itself, all of the same kind: a qa_script step and an acceptance criterion could not both be satisfied.

The comment the plan mandates was itself a hit. v2 also missed a second hit of the same kind: the release note's own FILENAME, upcoming-release-notes/remove-duplicate-weekly-end-date-suite.md, contains the token, and that file is neither plan/ nor the work order. The exemption now lives in step 3 alone and is expressed as a scoped command that the mandated comment and the release note filename cannot violate, rather than as an exemption list that has to be kept in step by step.

(2) v2's files[1] said to insert the comment 'using exactly the text supplied in the work order' but supplied no such text, while AC-2 pinned the comment's opening to a literal phrase files[1] never produced. An implementer following files[1] could not have satisfied AC-2. The comment's full text is now quoted verbatim in files[1], and it opens with exactly the phrase AC-2 requires, so no two artefacts can disagree about the first line.

(3) v2's AC-2.how_to_verify said the comparison is 'recorded verbatim' in the comment while files[1] described the content in prose, leaving the implementer to choose wording that AC-2's 'verbatim' would then judge. AC-2 now requires the block to match files[1]'s quoted text, so there is one text and both artefacts point at it.

The v1 objection, already fixed in v2, is kept: the full comparison lives in exactly one artefact (the code comment), and the release note is held only to the repo's own convention of one sentence.
